newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dachser integrates air, sea freight operations.
newsitem.headline: Dachser integrates air, sea freight operations.

text.p: German freight forwarder Dachser GmbH & Co. said it has integrated its air cargo and sea freight operations into a single department.
The Dachser Air & Sea Freight Division would sell services through 15 Germany offices in both areas of forwarding and seek synergy effects where possible, a company statement said.
Dachser spokesman Helmut Schwertler added: "Up to now, airfreight was separate but since both air and sea are intercontinental operations it makes sense to bring them together for synergy effects."
Sea freight had been sold as part of the overland forwarding service, he said.
Integration of air and sea services made particular sense for imports into Europe and Germany, which represented more business than exports, Schwertler said.
"Dachser is one of the few forwarders with its own land network in Europe so exports from the Far East, for example, can be combined," he explained.
Dachser, a family-owned company, is the exclusive Germany member of the forwarders grouping WACO and one of the top ten IATA air cargo forwarders in Germany.
The company generated turnover of 1.6 billion marks in 1995 and handled a total of 5.5 million tonnes, Dachser said.
It has eight foreign subsidiaries and holds stakes in forwarding companies in Hong Kong, Australia, South Africa and Finland. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
